title: 7 Days in Egypt: A Small-Group Itinerary
excerpt: A 7-day Egypt group tour from shared departures: two Cairo day tours plus a five-day Nile cruise, from €714 per person (Nov 2026). Plus two 5-day routes.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

Seven days in Egypt covers two bases: two full Cairo days for Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum and the older pyramid fields, then a five-day Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan. Sawa lists no 7-day package, so the week is assembled from three shared departures: from €714 per person for the guided parts, as listed in November 2026, plus your Cairo hotel and the flights. Only five days? Pick one of the two five-day routes further down instead.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

You have one week of holiday and the classic Egyptian dilemma: the pyramids of Cairo or a Nile cruise? A good 7-day Egypt group tour refuses to choose. Two well-planned Cairo days cover Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum and the older pyramid fields at Saqqara and Dahshur; a five-day cruise then carries you from Luxor to Aswan past Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu and Philae. This post assembles that week from shared departures listed by Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform, with prices and honest trade-offs. If you have only five days, the section on two five-day routes shows what to keep.

7 days in Egypt: the short answer

Seven days is enough for the headline route: two Cairo days, then five cruise days from Luxor to Aswan. You will see the three Giza pyramids and the Sphinx, the Grand Egyptian Museum, Djoser's Step Pyramid at Saqqara, the Bent and Red Pyramids at Dahshur, Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Philae. What one week cannot fit: Alexandria, the Red Sea, Abu Simbel at an easy pace, and Old Cairo's mosques and churches. Leave those for a second trip or a nine-day package.

No 7-day package exists: how the week is assembled

Honesty first: as listed in November 2026, Sawa has no 7-day package. The closest ready-made options on the itineraries page are the 4- and 5-day cruises, a 9-day Nile-and-Cairo package and a 12-day end-to-end trip. This week is therefore assembled from three separate shared departures: two Cairo day tours plus the Nile Majesty 5-day river cruise from Luxor. Each departure confirms independently when four travellers join. Reserve the cruise first, because it boards only on Mondays and Saturdays and anchors the calendar, then place the Cairo days in front of it.

Day by day: the 7-day plan at a glance

The plan needs one hotel base and one boat: three nights in Cairo, four aboard the cruise, and you leave from Aswan. Arrive in Cairo the evening before day 1.

Check the Nile Majesty page for the exact day-by-day content of your sailing.

The two Cairo days

Both Cairo days include hotel pickup. Day 1 is a guided walk among the pyramids of Khufu, Khafre and Menkaure, the panorama viewpoint and the Sphinx with its Valley Temple, then lunch and a guided visit to the Grand Egyptian Museum. The tour runs about 8 hours, and entrance tickets for both sites and lunch are included; pyramid interiors and camel rides are not. For the full detail on that day, see Pyramids and the Grand Egyptian Museum in one day.

Day 2 runs about nine hours through the older capitals: Memphis, Saqqara and Djoser's Step Pyramid, a lunch stop, then Dahshur's Bent and Red Pyramids. Tickets and lunch are included. Going inside the Red Pyramid is covered by the site ticket, and your guide advises on the day; the Serapeum at Saqqara is a separate ticket and is not included. Take the early night seriously: day 3 begins with a flight south, and Dahshur's open desert offers little shade at midday.

The five cruise days, Luxor to Aswan

Day 3 starts with the Cairo to Luxor flight, about an hour, and the Nile Majesty itinerary does the rest: Karnak's colonnades, then a carriage ride. Day 4 covers the West Bank's Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple and the Colossi of Memnon before the boat sails south. Day 5 brings Edfu and Kom Ombo; day 6, Philae, the High Dam and the Unfinished Obelisk; day 7, breakfast and leaving the boat in Aswan. The cruise is full board, with entrance tickets and a guide included; special tombs such as Tutankhamun's, drinks, tips, a balloon flight and insurance are not. Your group of up to 8 sails on a shared five-star ship and does the excursions together with its guide.

One rule makes the week work: the boat sets the calendar. Nile Majesty boards in Luxor on Mondays and Saturdays, so reserve that date first, then place the two Cairo day tours on the days before boarding.

What you can realistically skip in one week

One week means skipping real places, so skip them on purpose. Alexandria is a 10-hour day trip that would swallow a Cairo day; the Red Sea needs three more days to be worth it; Dendera and Abydos, the far temples north of Luxor, would add another day. The painful one is Old Cairo, with its Coptic churches, which only the 9-day package keeps. Three details help the rest go smoothly:

  • Book the cruise, then the Cairo days. A missed day tour can be rebooked; a missed cruise boarding cannot.
  • Three departures, three confirmations. Each needs its own four travellers, the GoAhead. A day tour has until seven days before to reach four; the cruise has until 30 days before. Watch the status of all three dates, and book flights only after each date confirms.
  • Leave Abu Simbel for day 8 if it matters. The temples sit about 280 km from Aswan by road, 3.5 to 4 hours each way, and the Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour runs about 9 hours with hotel pickup in Aswan, from €50, as listed in November 2026. It is a separate departure, so add an eighth night in Aswan rather than sprinting before a homeward flight.

Only five days? Two routes that work

Five days is enough for one Egyptian route done well, and not enough for two. What five days cannot absorb is a third destination: adding Hurghada or Abu Simbel turns a holiday into a transfer schedule. Two plans realistically fit.

Route A: Cairo and Luxor by day tours

Route A keeps the pyramids in play: two hotel bases, with shared day tours doing the driving. It is the five-day route for a first visit.

  1. Day 1: Giza. Giza Uncovered, about 4 hours: the Giza plateau ticket, the panorama viewpoint and the Great Sphinx, from €29 per person.
  2. Day 2: Giza's museum or the older pyramids. Secrets of the Grand Egyptian Museum, about 3 hours with general admission, from €48; or Memphis, Saqqara and Dahshur, about 9 hours, from €33.
  3. Day 3: Fly to Luxor. About an hour in the air; settle in, walk the riverside Corniche, and see Luxor Temple lit up after dark.
  4. Day 4: Both banks of Luxor. Luxor in Depth, about 9 hours with hotel pickup and a Nile crossing: Karnak, Luxor Temple, the Valley of the Kings, Hatshepsut's temple and the Colossi of Memnon, from €75. Special tombs such as Tutankhamun's are not included, and for lunch, check the departure page. (Nefertari's tomb has been closed since March 2024, so do not plan around it.)
  5. Day 5: Fly home from Luxor. With a late flight, the Dendera and Abydos temple day (about 9.5 hours, from €42) can fit beforehand, but only once that date has confirmed. The Dendera roof chapels and crypts are paid separately on site.

The day tours add up to from €152 per person (€29 + €48 + €75, as listed in November 2026), but that figure covers tours only. Route A's real budget also carries four hotel nights split between Cairo and Luxor, the domestic flight and most meals.

Route B: the Nile Majesty cruise on its own

Route B swaps roads and hotels for one boat: the five cruise days of the week plan above, from €610 per person, as listed in November 2026, with four nights' full board, entrance tickets and a guide. Choose it if you have seen Cairo or would rather unpack once. The trade-offs: the Giza pyramids lie a flight away in the wrong direction, and you must reach Luxor for a Monday or Saturday boarding.

Recommendation for five days: first trip with the pyramids non-negotiable? Take Route A. Already seen Cairo, or set on the river? Take Route B. Compare totals, not tour prices: Route A's tours exclude hotels, flights and most meals, while Route B's price includes a floating hotel and full board.

The honest trade-offs: assembled week vs the 9-day package

Assembling the week costs less but moves the logistics onto you. The guided parts cost from €714 per person in total (€71 + €33 + €610, as listed in November 2026), but the Cairo hotel, both domestic flights, drinks and tips are yours to arrange. The 9-day Egypt in Depth package bundles four Cairo hotel nights, both domestic flights and Old Cairo into one booking, from €1,403 per person.

Domestic flights Not included Cairo to Luxor and Aswan to Cairo included
Cairo hotel Book it yourself 4 nights included, in three comfort tiers
Old Cairo Skipped Included
Cruise 4 nights, Luxor to Aswan 4 nights, Luxor to Aswan

Recommendation: assemble the seven days if you like controlling your own flights and hotels and are happy watching three dates fill; take the 9-day package if you would rather handle logistics once and keep Old Cairo. Either way, budget beyond the tour prices: three Cairo hotel nights, drinks on board and tipping. Day tours have no solo surcharge; on the cruise, solo cabins are confirmed in the booking, so check before you reserve.

How to do the week with Sawa Tours

Sawa Tours is an Egypt shared-departure platform, operated by Online Era (registration 148500). It runs a fixed catalogue: Sawa sets the calendar and the prices, and travellers booked through several selling agencies share one tour, one date, one guide and one price, never more than eight to a group. Prices are fixed per traveller. Reserving a seat is free and needs no card, and nothing is charged before the GoAhead, the moment four travellers (people, not bookings) have reserved the date. The two kinds of departure in this week have different terms:

  • Day tours. A 10% deposit at the GoAhead, the balance two days (48 hours) before departure. A forming date has until seven days before to reach four; otherwise it is cancelled, nothing is charged and another date is suggested. Cancel at least 48 hours before for a full refund; under 48 hours, the 10% deposit is retained.
  • The cruise. A 25% deposit at the GoAhead, the balance 14 days before departure, and four travellers needed by 30 days before. Cancel 30 or more days before at no charge; from 29 to 15 days, half the deposit (12.5%) is charged; at 14 days or fewer, or on a no-show, the deposit (25%) is retained. Some components, such as cabins, may become non-refundable earlier; that is disclosed before you pay.

On both, force majeure means a full refund, a traveller who does not pay after the GoAhead is excluded and the tour still runs, and a confirmed date is not cancelled for low numbers. The full rules are in the terms, and the mechanics are covered in how the GoAhead works.

Payments go through a secure payment link from Online Era (General Sales Agent licence 32241); charges are in euros. Each departure is operated by one of the licensed Egyptian agencies with travellers on the date, named before the deposit is due. Sawa's founding operating partner is Capital Travel Service (licence 2179). Choose your pieces on the itineraries page, then browse forming departures and reserve. Questions go to WhatsApp at +20 109 284 7613, answered 24/7 while your tour is running.

The verdict on one week in Egypt

Seven days works when the cruise sets the schedule: two Cairo days for Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum and Saqqara, then five days on the river from Luxor to Aswan, and the discipline to skip the rest. With five days, pick one of the two routes instead of squeezing both. Next step: reserve a date on the Nile Majesty cruise from Luxor, then build the Cairo days around it using the itineraries page. Reserving a seat is free.

faq.q: Is 7 days in Egypt enough for a first visit?
faq.a: For the headline route, yes. Seven days covers Giza and the Grand Egyptian Museum, the older pyramid fields at Saqqara and Dahshur, and a complete Luxor-to-Aswan cruise with Karnak, the Valley of the Kings, Edfu, Kom Ombo and Philae. What does not fit: Alexandria, the Red Sea, Abu Simbel at an easy pace and Old Cairo. Stretch to nine days or keep a list for a second trip.

Yes, if you choose one route. Cairo plus Luxor by day tours costs from €152 per person in tours, plus hotels and a domestic flight; the Nile Majesty cruise from Luxor to Aswan costs from €610 per person with full board, as listed in November 2026. Adding a third destination in five days turns the trip into transfers.

faq.q: Which day should the Nile cruise start on?
faq.a: Around the boat, not the tours. Nile Majesty boards in Luxor on Mondays and Saturdays, as listed in November 2026. If you board on a Saturday, for example, tour Cairo on Thursday and Friday and fly south on Saturday morning, provided the day tours have dates on those days. Reserve the cruise date first, because it is the least flexible piece.

faq.q: How much does one week in Egypt cost on this plan?
faq.a: The guided parts total from €714 per person: the Giza and Grand Egyptian Museum day from €71, Memphis, Saqqara and Dahshur from €33, and the five-day full-board cruise from €610, as listed in November 2026. Add your international flights, a Cairo hotel, the domestic flights, insurance, drinks and tips.

faq.q: Do I have to book the tours and cruise as one package?
faq.a: No, and Sawa has no 7-day package to book. Each piece is an independent shared departure with its own date and its own fixed price, and each confirms on its own four travellers. Reserve the cruise first for its fixed boarding days, then add the Cairo day tours in front of it. Nothing is charged for any date until it reaches four travellers.

faq.q: What happens if one of the three departures never fills?
faq.a: You pay nothing for that date. A day tour that has not reached four by seven days before is cancelled, and a cruise that has not reached four by 30 days before is cancelled, with nothing charged and Sawa suggesting other dates. Once a date is confirmed, it is not cancelled for low numbers. With three separate departures in one week, book flights only after each date confirms.

faq.q: Can Abu Simbel fit inside the 7 days?
faq.a: Not comfortably. You leave the boat on day 7 in Aswan, and the Abu Simbel day tour runs about nine hours, from €50 per person, because the temples are 3.5 to 4 hours from Aswan by road each way. The calmer plan is an eighth night in Aswan and the tour the next day.
